public_body: Pioneer Valley Performing Arts Charter School Board Of Trustees
overall: Violation found for posting notice under 48 hours before the November 21 remote meeting and for admitting the public about 20 minutes late; the executive session topic description, transcript access, and minute forwarding complaints were not violations, and the other allegations were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board was biased in choosing which public written submissions were attached to the October 21 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: There is nothing within the Open Meeting Law that requires a public body to attach written submissions to the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged notice of the November 21 special remote meeting was not posted at least 48 hours in advance.
allegations.key_passage: Because notice was not posted 48 hours in advance of the meeting, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the late-notice violation was intentional; the AG declined to find intentional conduct.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find the violation intentional.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the remote November 21 meeting was not accessible to the public until about 20 minutes after the posted start time.
allegations.key_passage: does not excuse the Board from the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the executive session topic in the November 21 notice misstated the purpose, referencing collective bargaining and minutes review.
allegations.key_passage: The description of the executive session therefore complied with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a real-time transcript of the November 21 executive session was available to the public through a link in the Zoom chat.
allegations.key_passage: Even if taken as true, the complainant’s allegation regarding the accidental public generation of an executive session transcript in real time does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged board members received prior executive session minutes, with instructions to delete them after reading, including members who joined later.
allegations.key_passage: Similarly, the forwarding of unreleased executive session minutes to new members of the Board does not implicate any provision of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
All members of the Board attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by the AG's office within 90 days and certify to the office that they have done so.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and we caution the Board that a future finding of an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
